smells.finding: The longest new unit is _assert_every_populated_field_renders (~34 lines including comments, ~18 lines of code) and _fully_populated_gate (~27 lines, almost all fixture assignment). Both are single-purpose and read top-to-bottom. The rewrite in fact SHORTENS the previously monolithic test method by extracting these two helpers.
TaskFieldCompleteness grows to ~215 lines: a ~40-line class docstring, a 23-line commented exclusion set, three helpers and three tests.

override.repo_standard: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Verification Discipline' (a check must be demonstrated capable of failing, and the demonstration is part of the deliverable) plus the g2-implement handoff constraint 'Match the test module's idiom and comment density'; the surrounding module (RenderAnchorsAndConstraints, Inv1CompletenessOracle, GoldenOutputBriefing) uses the same long-docstring, one-property-per-class shape.
override.reason: The class is ONE property plus the machinery that proves the property can fail. Splitting the fixture, the assertion helper and the negative self-test into separate classes would put the falsifiability proof at a distance from the thing it falsifies, which is the exact separation that let #420's version report green. Size here is doctrine-mandated evidence, not accreted responsibility.

smells.finding: The change REMOVES duplication rather than adding it: the fixture and the assertion path are extracted into _fully_populated_gate() and _assert_every_populated_field_renders(), and all three tests drive those same objects. override.repo_standard: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Verification Discipline': 'Define a guard by its consumer's behaviour, not by a hand-maintained list. A list of characters, filenames or call sites drifts from the predicate the code actually applies, and the gap is silent.'
override.reason: The builder IS the canonical Task enumeration; asking it for its keys is the standard's prescribed form, and re-listing them in the test would be exactly the hand-maintained list the standard forbids. docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Task table -- the only public alternative -- is hand-authored prose and is currently stale on the `directives` row, so cutting the guard against it would weaken it. smells.finding: No repeated parameter group appears. The (t, out) pair passed to _assert_every_populated_field_renders is a task and its rendering, used once.

The ledger is two sets of field-name strings compared with assertEqual. A field name is genuinely a string here (it is a dict key of the Task shape), and set difference is what produces the by-name failure message the handoff requires.
Widest new signature is _assert_every_populated_field_renders(self, t, out) -- two arguments. _leaf_texts takes one.
After this change, adding a field to the engine's Task shape requires a matching edit in this test class's fixture (or its exclusion set) -- one change now demands two edits.

override.reason: The forced second edit IS the guard. Without it the loop runs over the fixture's keys, a new engine field is absent from the loop, absent from the ledger's expected set, and passes green -- the exact forgetting failure this class exists to catch. The failure message names the field and states both remedies, so the second edit is directed rather than discovered.
